findings.location: blockquote.lyrics — stanza 3, line 'Angels to beckon me'
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the line faithfully into Greek conveying the meaning 'Angels to beckon me' (i.e., angels summoning/beckoning the singer nearer). Preserve the hymn sense and meter but do not introduce new actions (such as killing). Example: «Άγγελοι να με κελεύσουν» or «Άγγελοι να με προσκαλέσουν». Replace the existing incorrect text: «Άγγελοι να με σκοτώσουν—όχι––να με κινήσουν— να με καλούν» with a faithful translation like «Άγγελοι να μου γνέψουν».
findings.translation_quote: Άγγελοι να με σκοτώσουν—όχι––να με κινήσουν— να με καλούν

findings.location: multiple paragraphs quoting hymn title (e.g., 'Nearer, My God to Thee' in Boston Peace Jubilee paragraph and elsewhere)
findings.suggested_fix: Quoted substantive English prose (including hymn titles that are part of the printed authoritative text) must be translated into the target language. Replace the English title occurrences with a faithful Greek rendering used consistently throughout the article (for example: «Κοντύτερα, Θεέ μου, σε Σένα» or another literal, idiomatic Greek equivalent). Ensure every instance of the hymn title and any other quoted English substantive phrases are translated.
findings.translation_quote: «Nearer, My God to Thee»; «Nearer, my God, to Thee,»

findings.source_quote: her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis
findings.suggested_fix: The translator rendered 'consumption' as 'καχεξία, γνωστή σήμερα ως φυματίωση', which implies cachexia and is misleading. Use a phrasing that correctly identifies 'consumption' as tuberculosis in modern terms, for example: «πέθανε από την ασθένεια που τότε ονομάζονταν 'consumption' — σήμερα γνωστή ως φυματίωση.» Or simply: «πέθανε από φυματίωση (τότε ονομάζονταν 'consumption').»
findings.translation_quote: πέθανε από καχεξία, γνωστή σήμερα ως φυματίωση

findings.location: blockquote.lyrics — stanza 1 punctuation and stanza 4 'Bethel I’ll raise' translation
findings.source_quote:
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the question mark which alters tone and possibly meaning. Render without interrogative punctuation and ensure 'That raiseth me' is translated as causative (that lifts or exalts me). Example: «Ακόμη κι αν είναι σταυρός / Που με ανυψώνει,» (with a comma). For 'Bethel I'll raise' ensure idiomatic Greek capturing the idea 'I will raise a Bethel (a memorial) out of my stony griefs' — e.g., «Από τις πετρώδεις λύπες μου θα υψώσω ένα Βηθὲλ» rather than the current phrasing with a question mark and ‹Θα ανυψώσω ένα Βηθέλ;› punctuation.
findings.translation_quote:
Ακόμη κι αν είναι ένας σταυρός
Που με ανυψώνει; / Θα ανυψώσω ένα Βηθέλ;
